record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares image-classification accuracy across architectures and reports optimizer comparisons using a different recipe from the versions’ original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model and optimizer results that bear on V3 and V4. Its fixed dropout rate is not ablated; it reports no random-label, width, batch-size, sharpness, or memorized-example results.
record.test_reason: The AdamW-to-SGD intervention tests V4's switching clause through held-out accuracy comparisons with AdamW alone. The MLP-Mixer comparison does not directly test V3's claim about fully connected networks: Mixer uses separate, shared token-mixing and channel-mixing MLPs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that CXV combines convolutional priors and linear attention for low-resource image classification, and that switching optimizers improves accuracy across architectures. They explicitly call for further investigation of initialization, hyperparameters, learning rates, and optimizer choices.
record.recipe_differences: Compares image-classification architectures and a two-phase AdamW-to-SGD training method; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ original interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and dataset change the reported accuracy; the paper also reports optimizer-phase changes, but no matched training-versus-test gap measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-34 exceeds parameter-matched MLP Mixer-5 accuracy on CIFAR-10 (87.97 versus 60.26), CIFAR-100 (56.05 versus 34.81), and Tiny ImageNet (42.65 versus 20.26).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A CNN outperforms a structured all-MLP token mixer under this low-resource training recipe.

record.problems: The architecture comparison uses MLP Mixer-5 against ResNet-34, which differ in parameter count; several reported model parameter counts are not stated individually. Accuracy is reported as best of three runs without uncertainty estimates. The optimizer table compares DualOpT with AdamW but does not give SGD-only numbers.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width-dependent generalization beyond zero training error.
CNN versus conventional fully connected networks; isolation of local connectivity; learned sparse connections and convolutional initialization.

The ordering of SGD alone versus AdamW alone; matched training performance; limited versus broader tuning; decoupled weight decay ablation; language benchmarks. Switching is tested with AdamW rather than Adam, without a documented matched training budget.
Batch-size effects under fixed epochs and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects: dropout is fixed at 0.5 without an ablation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All reported accuracies are best of three runs, without uncertainty estimates. Switching follows 20 epochs of stagnant accuracy and adds an SGD phase; matched total training budgets are not documented. The text says DualOpT also exceeds SGD alone but supplies no SGD-only values, so it cannot establish AdamW-versus-SGD ordering.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label generalization.
No width sweep or test-error measurement around or beyond an interpolation threshold.
The comparison is against MLP-Mixer, not a conventional fully connected network; the paper does not isolate local connectivity or test learned sparse connections or convolutional initialization.
No reported direct held-out comparison of AdamW alone with SGD alone; broader tuning, language benchmarks, and decoupled weight decay comparisons are not tested.
No large-batch comparison or batch-size sweep.
Dropout is set to 0.5 across models, with no dropout ablation or training-set-size comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization measure is evaluated.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining experiment.
